rows: A fixed amount you must pay before the insurer pays any admissible claim. In indemnity plans, it is a rupee. [3]
The insurer starts paying paying only after deductible is crossed.
A percentage of the admissible claim that you must bear. It does not reduce the sum insured, but reduces what insurer pays pays for that claim.
You share the bill in a fixed ratio, such as 0% or20%.

A period after policy start during which certain claims are not payable. Standard policies generally have30-day initial waiting period, and pre-existing-disease waiting are commonly cappedat36months in newerIRDA-regulated-products[7]
Claims during the waiting period may be fully rejected.
A cap on hospital room charge covered by the policy, often linked to a percentage of the sum insured.[2]
If you choose alier room, some policies reduce payment for other hospital charges in the same proportion.
Treatments or situations the policy does not cover at all, such as pre-existing-existing disease during the waiting period, many non-medical items, cosmetic, care, and other listed exclusions.[132]
The insurer pays nothing for excluded items or events.
